record.paper_title: Relativistic jets in narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
record.original_question: Only a small fraction of narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies are radio-loud, and radio-loudness in this context is discussed in terms of the ratio of rest-frame 1.4 GHz to 4400 Å flux density. What is the origin of radio-loudness in narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies, especially in the gamma-ray-emitting subset?

evidence.quote: What is the origin of the radio-loudness?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the population of narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLS1) galaxies, a class of active galactic nuclei (AGN) characterized by relatively narrow permitted optical emission lines (with broad-line region Hβ FWHM ≲ 2000 km/s), strong Fe II multiplets, and weak [O III] emission, typically hosting black holes of comparatively low mass accreting at high Eddington ratios. For an AGN, define the radio-loudness parameter as the ratio R = F_{1.4 GHz} / F_{4400 Å} of the rest-frame flux density at 1.4 GHz to that at 4400 Å, and call the source radio-loud when R exceeds the conventional threshold (e.g., R > 10). Empirically, only a small fraction of NLS1 galaxies are radio-loud, and within that fraction a still smaller subset has been detected as persistent γ-ray emitters by Fermi/LAT, indicating the presence of a closely aligned relativistic jet.

Problem: Identify and characterize the physical origin of radio-loudness in NLS1 galaxies, and in particular determine the mechanism(s) responsible for the launching of powerful relativistic jets in the γ-ray-emitting subset. Specifically, explain which combination of central black hole mass, spin, accretion mode and rate, host-galaxy properties, and circumnuclear environment selects the rare NLS1 galaxies that develop radio-loud, jetted activity, and account for why the bulk of the NLS1 population (with otherwise similar nuclear properties) remains radio-quiet.
artifact.category_tag: Active galactic nuclei and relativistic jets
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2018–2019 reviews and observational studies) continues to treat the origin of radio-loudness in NLS1 galaxies, and in particular jet formation in their γ-ray-emitting subset, as an open question. Authors emphasize that NLS1 hosts (often late-type galaxies with low-mass black holes) challenge standard jet-formation paradigms and that the disc/jet connection, role of black hole spin/mass, and host-galaxy environment remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic Jets in Gamma-Ray-Emitting Narrow-Line Seyfert 1 Galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: NLS1 hosted in late-type galaxies with relatively small black hole masses opened new challenging questions about the nature of these objects, the disc/jet connection, the emission mechanisms at high energies, and the formation of relativistic jets.
status_evidence.claim: The origin of jets in radio-loud, gamma-ray NLS1 galaxies remains an open research question.

status_evidence.title: Radio and gamma-ray loud narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies in the spotlight
status_evidence.snippet: Review of properties of radio-loud and gamma-ray emitting NLS1s, highlighting unresolved issues regarding their jet launching mechanisms.
status_evidence.claim: Radio-loudness origin in NLS1s is still actively investigated.
